rejected.reason: Affirmative 'could' is used for general past permission, not for permission on one specific occasion ('yesterday'), where 'were allowed to' is needed.
Nothing in the sentence forces an obligation, so 'can' and 'may' (customers are allowed to pay first) also give a correct, meaningful sentence.
